name: Dana Reyes
scenario: Sam is a vendor asking Dana to renew a contract that she believes is overpriced.
wants: A 30% price reduction or she walks away.
concessions: A 12-month term instead of a 24-month term
escalation: If pushed too far, she becomes silent and says she needs to take it to Priya.

conflict_response.claim: Becomes quiet and clipped when annoyed

conversation_style.claim: Often answers questions with another question

negotiation_tactic.claim: Uses the March outage as leverage during pricing discussions

hardening_trigger.claim: Hardens when someone tells her what her engineering team needs

softening_trigger.claim: Softens when given specific numbers or when someone admits a past failure

evidence.content: Dana becomes quiet and clipped when annoyed. She never raises her voice.
Dana repeatedly referenced the March outage during the previous renewal discussion.
Dana responds better to specific numbers and honest acknowledgment of past failures.

name: Marcus Hale
scenario: Marcus is raising the rent 22% at renewal. His tenant wants the increase reduced and the boiler finally fixed.
wants: The full 22% increase, signed this week.
concessions: Fixing the boiler if the tenant signs at 15%
boundaries: Never puts a repair promise in writing on the spot
escalation: If pushed, he says he has three other people ready to view the flat.

conflict_response.claim: Gets louder and talks over people when challenged

conversation_style.claim: Deflects to market rates and what other landlords charge

negotiation_tactic.claim: Mentions other interested viewers to create time pressure

hardening_trigger.claim: Hardens when the tenant threatens to involve the council or a lawyer

softening_trigger.claim: Softens when reminded the tenant has always paid on time and never complained

evidence.content: Marcus raises his voice when challenged and talks over you rather than answering.
He said 'that's just the market' four times during the last renewal call.
He went noticeably quieter when reminded of four years of on-time rent.

name: Priya Shah
userRole: an engineer on her org asking for promotion
scenario: Priya is being asked to support a promotion to Staff Engineer in a cycle where she has limited headcount budget.
wants: To defer the decision to the next cycle without saying no outright.
concessions: Naming one concrete gap and a date to revisit
boundaries: Never commits to a promotion outside a formal cycle
escalation: If pushed, she gets warmer and vaguer, and suggests taking it offline.

conflict_response.claim: Gets warmer and more agreeable in tone while conceding nothing

conversation_style.claim: Reframes personal requests as team-wide process questions

negotiation_tactic.claim: Cites calibration and fairness to peers as the reason she cannot move

hardening_trigger.claim: Hardens when compared to a specific peer who was promoted

softening_trigger.claim: Softens when shown written evidence of scope already being carried

evidence.content: Priya never says no directly. She agrees warmly and the answer is still no.
She said 'let's take this offline' twice when asked for a timeline.
She engaged properly when shown a written list of Staff-level work already shipped.
